faqs.question: What is a visual field test?
faqs.answer: A visual field test (perimetry) measures your entire scope of vision — both central and peripheral (side) vision. It maps areas of vision loss (scotomas) that you may not have noticed. It is essential for diagnosing and monitoring glaucoma, neurological conditions affecting vision, and certain retinal diseases.

faqs.question: How is a visual field test performed?
faqs.answer: You sit at the perimeter machine and look at a central fixation point. Small lights of varying brightness appear in different areas of your peripheral vision. You press a button each time you see a light. The machine maps which areas you can and cannot see, creating a detailed map of your visual field.

faqs.question: How long does visual field testing take?
faqs.answer: A standard visual field test takes about 5–10 minutes per eye. More detailed or specialized testing may take 15 minutes per eye. It requires concentration and cooperation — the technician will guide you through the process.

whatIsIt: Visual Field Testing (Perimetry) is a specialized diagnostic exam that precisely maps your entire field of vision, including your central and peripheral (side) sight. By asking you to respond to small flashes of light of varying intensities, the machine identifies exactly where your vision is intact and where you have 'blind spots' (scotomas). This testing is available at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care and is crucial for detecting diseases that slowly steal side vision.
whyItIsDone: To detect the subtle, early loss of peripheral vision that is the hallmark of Glaucoma
To map the specific visual field defects caused by neurological issues like a stroke or brain tumor
To evaluate the visual impact of an inflamed or compressed optic nerve (optic neuritis)
To monitor whether a known eye or brain condition is worsening over time or stabilizing with treatment

procedureSteps.title: Setup
procedureSteps.description: You sit comfortably at the perimeter machine. One eye is patched. Your chin and forehead are positioned against supports. The room lighting is standardized.

items: The technician explains the procedure: keep looking at the central orange fixation light at all times. Small white lights will flash at various locations and brightness levels throughout your visual field.
Press the button each time you see a light — even if it's very dim
It's normal to miss some lights — the machine is testing your threshold
Don't look around for lights — keep your eyes fixed on the central target

procedureSteps.title: Testing
procedureSteps.description: The automated program presents lights at various locations in your visual field. You respond to each light you see. The machine adjusts light intensity to determine the threshold of visibility at each point. A typical test takes 5–10 minutes per eye.

items: The machine generates detailed maps and statistical analyses including mean deviation, pattern standard deviation, and glaucoma hemifield test. Dr. Dibya Prabha reviews the results, compares them to any previous tests, and integrates the findings with your complete eye examination and OCT results.

preparation: No special preparation is needed — you can eat, drink, and take medications normally
Bring your current glasses — you'll wear them during the test if needed (near correction for the central target)
Get a good night's sleep — fatigue affects concentration and test reliability
The test requires concentration — if you're not feeling well, consider rescheduling
A practice test may be run first to familiarize you with the process

faqs.question: What is retinal laser treatment?
faqs.answer: Retinal laser treatment (laser photocoagulation) uses a focused beam of light to create tiny, controlled burns on the retina. These burns seal leaking blood vessels in diabetic retinopathy, create a barrier around retinal tears to prevent detachment, or reduce abnormal blood vessel growth. It is a proven, effective treatment performed in the clinic — no hospital stay needed.

faqs.question: Is retinal laser painful?
faqs.answer: Most patients experience mild discomfort — a sensation of brief, bright flashes and sometimes a mild aching sensation. Numbing eye drops are used. The procedure is generally well-tolerated. For more extensive treatment (pan-retinal photocoagulation), the procedure may be divided into multiple sessions for comfort.

whatIsIt: Retinal Laser Treatment (Photocoagulation) is a highly precise, outpatient medical procedure utilized by Dr. Dibya Prabha to treat various severe retinal conditions. A finely focused beam of light is used to create microscopic thermal burns on the retina. These strategic burns can seal leaking blood vessels, destroy abnormal new vessel growth, or effectively 'weld' a torn retina to the underlying tissue to prevent a catastrophic detachment.
whyItIsDone: To urgently seal a retinal tear or hole, completely preventing a full retinal detachment
To stop the leaking of fluid from damaged blood vessels in Diabetic Macular Edema
To purposefully destroy the oxygen-starved peripheral retina (Panretinal Photocoagulation) in advanced Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy, forcing abnormal blood vessels to shrink
To treat complications following a retinal vein occlusion (eye stroke)

items: Numbing eye drops are instilled to ensure comfort. A special contact lens is placed on the eye with lubricating gel to focus the laser beam precisely on the retina. The procedure is performed with you seated comfortably at the slit lamp.
Dr. Dibya Prabha delivers laser spots to the targeted areas of the retina. You will see brief, bright flashes and may feel a mild sensation — most patients tolerate this well.

The number of laser spots varies by condition: from a few dozen spots for a small retinal tear, to several hundred spots over multiple sessions for pan-retinal photocoagulation. Each session typically lasts 10–30 minutes.

procedureSteps.title: Completion
procedureSteps.description: The contact lens is removed. Your vision will be blurry for a few hours from the bright lights and gel. You can go home immediately. Arrange for someone to drive you if extensive laser was performed.

procedureSteps.title: Follow-up
procedureSteps.description: Dr. Dibya Prabha schedules follow-up visits to assess the laser effect — typically 2–4 weeks after treatment. Additional laser sessions may be needed depending on the condition and response.

preparation: No special preparation is needed for most retinal laser procedures
If extensive laser (PRP) is planned, arrange for someone to drive you home — your vision will be temporarily blurred
Take your regular medications unless instructed otherwise
Inform Dr. Prabha of all medications, especially blood thinners (though these usually do not need to be stopped)
Bring sunglasses for after the procedure
